reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (rubric-reviewer agent), scoring as Dr. Elena Vasquez
scope: Narration is the spoken > lines of s5_ai/script.md (8 scenes; text unchanged since the 2026-10-23 review), with s4_analytics/script.md as the also story, where evidence caps a verdict at partial. Screen verdicts are judged on the 8 scenes of s5_ai/deck_anim.html and the eight qlik_panels/*.png they embed, each opened and looked at, and on frames pulled from the finished C:\Claude\MCG Demo\05_MCG_AI_Outcomes_1080p.mp4 (3:31.8: a 3.0 s opening sting, the 203.8 s body, a 5.0 s end sting). This cut was rebuilt from the same capture with each scene anchored at its own slide change: line 1, 'Story four of four', now plays over the sc1 title slide and its Predict panel (on screen 3.0-7.25 s) instead of the sc2 heading, and every line starts about 0.3-0.6 s after its own slide. The closing slide holds past the last word (about 204.6 s) until the end sting at 206.75 s.
note: Ingrid, the re-cut puts the opening line on the title slide, so the Qlik Predict screen is now up for about four seconds instead of flashing past before anyone speaks; but it is the analytics video's panel, nobody mentions it, and still no scene shows an AI system acting on our tenant. The words are exactly the ones I failed earlier today, so my verdicts stand: the coding-agent loop is accountable and reversible, but preview is never said aloud, the Discovery Agent's alert reaches no named person, nothing on the consumption side has an approver, and citations and MCP exist only in story three. Six of the seven musts are open, and I would not put this pillar in front of the board or the NVWA as it stands.

verdicts.evidence: The sc1 panel is the Qlik Predict 'ML experiment' page on the live tenant: a model-metrics table of about thirty Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes and LightGBM runs (best F1 0.144), SHAP importance for route_id, warehouse_id and battery_level_pct, and a ROC curve, captioned 'Qlik Predict - models trained on governed data, scored and compared'. In this cut it is on screen from 3.0 s to 7.25 s under 'Story four of four: AI and Outcomes'; as rendered the table figures are too small to read and the confusion-matrix and bias-detection blocks fall below the frame.
verdicts.gap: It is the analytics video's own panel (s4_analytics embeds the same v5_predict_coldchain.png), the narration over it never refers to it, and it shows models being trained, not an AI acting on governed data. No scene shows an Answers response with its citation, an agent conversation, the Discovery Agent's configuration or a coding-agent session; v4_answers.png exists in qlik_panels and this deck does not embed it. The sc3 YAML diff and 'Problems: 0' chain are drawn HTML over v2_pipelines.png, two project cards (MCG Supply Chain Pipeline, olh_mcg_demo_cdc), neither of them the mcg-batch-pipeline the code header names. sc4's 'What the Discovery Agent watches' is v3_dataquality.png, Qlik's stock semantic types, every one created by Qlik on Jul 29, 2025. sc6's agentic route sits on a list of three source connections. The only AI output on our own data is sc8's small-print 'Generated by AI on October 23, 2026 at 6:45 PM' over the Supply Chain Health description, with no reviewer and the owner shown as Robert Schoenfeld rather than Henrik Jansen. Seven of the eight panels are reused from stories one to three; only automations.png is this video's own.

verdicts.evidence: It cites the NinjaVan contract amendment, effective the first of October
verdicts.gap: Video 05 never says that an answer cites a source. Its only words on Answers are 'Ask a question, get an answer', with a pointer back to story three, so a viewer of this video alone hears about AI answering questions with no citation at all. The NinjaVan example exists only in the analytics narration, and none of the eight panels here is an Answers response.

verdicts.evidence: through the Qlik MCP server — an assistant calling live Qlik tools to create the sheet
verdicts.gap: The AI video never mentions MCP. In the analytics video the Qlik MCP server is only the channel one assistant used to author sheets. Nobody says that any MCP-compatible assistant, not only Qlik's, can reach the governed data products, quality metrics, lineage and catalog, or that permissions, trust scores and draft status travel with them, so the interoperability claim that stops this reading as a closed vendor stack is never made.

verdicts.evidence: trust score falling below zero point seven, sync lag over an hour, volume moving more than fifty percent
verdicts.gap: The thresholds land; the recipient does not. 'Seventy-two silent hours becomes an alert', but no product owner, steward, channel or role is named as its reader: the two owners in our own material, Henrik Jansen for Supply Chain Health and Sophie Müller for Last Mile Performance, are never mentioned. 'Can watch' leaves open whether the agent is actually configured on these products, and the sc4 panel shows no agent configuration. The 0.7 threshold is on a different scale from the Trust Score the closing panel shows (3.8 / 5), so a viewer cannot tell what would trip it.

verdicts.evidence: Generated terms arrive in draft status and wait for a human to approve them.
verdicts.gap: Gates are named for three build-side actions only: the coding agent ('The human owns the decision'), glossary drafts, and low-confidence addresses ('to a human steward'). No approver is named for the Data Product Agent packaging products, the Data Quality Agent turning a sentence into an enforced rule, the Discovery Agent's alert, or the automations: 'except the one step that should stay human' never says which step, or whose. Nothing is gated on the consumption side; in the analytics video a sentence of plain English 'can end up as a governed object in a governed app' with no reviewer. Every approver is 'a human' or a steward, never a role with sign-off authority. On screen, sc5's glossary shows every visible term in Draft with the Stewards column empty, and sc8's AI-generated description carries no review.

Neither the AI nor the analytics narration says the word 'preview'. Declarative pipelines ('just YAML in a git repository'), the agentic route and sheet authoring over the Qlik MCP server are all presented as working capability. The only preview label is the sc6 footer 'Preview / roadmap', small print the criterion excludes. The one honesty line that is spoken, 'Qlik Answers capabilities, not separate products', is about packaging, not release status.

verdicts.evidence: And the model can run in your own tenant.
verdicts.gap: Said once, for the address route only, and as an option ('can run'), not as how Meridian runs it. Nothing says where customer data goes: the quoted 'the language model never leaves our infrastructure' is about the model, not the data, and is framed as what a buyer wants to hear. A Qlik Cloud tenant is hosted by Qlik, so 'your own tenant' and 'our infrastructure' are not the same thing, and the narration blurs them. Nothing says where the coding agent, the governance agents or Answers send prompts and data.

verdicts.evidence: the build side produces trust, and the consumption side spends it.
verdicts.gap: A slogan, not a demonstration. The two gold products are tied only to the agents ('what the agents operate on'); no consumption surface in this video is shown or said to read Supply Chain Health or Last Mile Performance. The one worked Answers example, in the analytics video, reads twenty-five operational documents, not the gold products. The sc2 caption repeats the line over the data-products list, but on screen only. A viewer is told that trust is spent but never who spends it, or on which product.

verdicts.evidence: The agent does the typing. The schema catches the mistakes. The human owns the decision. And if it is wrong, it is a git revert.
verdicts.gap: The narration is complete. On screen, the YAML diff and the schema check are drawn rather than captured, over two project cards that are not the mcg-batch-pipeline the code header names, and the drawn diff omits the timeBasedScheduling/schedule nesting the real file has. The repo's MCG CRM Landing schedule.yaml still reads INTERVAL=15 ('every 15 minutes'), so there is no commit of the 30-minute change and no record of who approved it.
